paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: holiness isn't a feeling, it's a whole way of living. God opens with "Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy." (Leviticus 19:2) Then He spends the rest of the chapter showing what that looks like on a regular Tuesday: how you treat your parents, your workers, your neighbors, the foreigner, even your scales. Nothing in a holy life is too small for God to care about. I mean NOTHING. Not even the measuring cup.

Notice how often God says "I am the LORD." He says it again and again, because every command rests on who He is, not on a rule book. Honest scales, fair courts, leftover grapes for the poor, and a straight word to a neighbor instead of hatred tucked away in your heart (Leviticus 19:17) all come from the same place. Then He sums up the whole run of neighbor commands: "love your neighbor as yourself." (Leviticus 19:18) Jesus later calls that the second command, right behind loving God (Matthew 22:37-39). And God ties the foreigner to His own people's story: "for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt." (Leviticus 19:34)

So what does this mean for you, baker? God's people are marked by how they love the people right in front of them, and that takes more than a good heart on Sunday. Think of the group chat, the paycheck, the grudge, the person nobody else is looking out for. Even in the hard case where a man sins, God provides a ram and promises he "will be forgiven" (Leviticus 19:22). I know a little something about being picked up when you thought you were done, friend, and He makes holy people out of folks like us. The story isn't over, because God isn't done teaching His people to be holy.
